title: Ezra's Commission
overview: Ezra Chapter 7 details the commissioning of Ezra, a skilled scribe and priest, during the reign of Artaxerxes, king of Persia. This chapter highlights Ezra's priestly lineage, his dedication to the Law of Moses, and the king's generous support for his mission to restore proper worship and governance in Jerusalem. The chapter emphasizes God's providential hand in granting Ezra favor and authority to lead a group of Israelites back to Jerusalem, equipped with resources to rebuild the temple services and enforce God's statutes. This chapter is pivotal in the book of Ezra as it marks the beginning of a renewed spiritual and civil reform under Ezra's leadership, reinforcing the centrality of the Mosaic Law in post-exilic Israel.
structure:
**Verses 1-5: Ezra’s Genealogy and Priesthood.** The chapter opens by establishing Ezra’s priestly heritage, tracing his lineage back to Aaron, underscoring his legitimate authority as a religious leader.

**Verses 6-10: Ezra’s Character and Journey.** Ezra is introduced as a skilled scribe devoted to the Law of Moses, who prepares his heart to seek, do, and teach God’s law. His journey from Babylon to Jerusalem is described, emphasizing God’s providential guidance.

**Verses 11-26: The King’s Decree and Instructions.** A detailed copy of King Artaxerxes’ official letter is presented, granting Ezra authority to lead the return, carry offerings, and appoint magistrates and judges. The decree ensures support and protection for Ezra and his mission.

**Verses 27-28: Ezra’s Praise and Strength.** The chapter concludes with Ezra’s blessing of God for moving the king’s heart and strengthening him to gather leaders for the journey, highlighting divine empowerment for the task.

keyVerses.text: This Ezra went up from Babylon; and he was a ready scribe in the law of Moses, which the LORD God of Israel had given: and the king granted him all his request, according to the hand of the LORD his God upon him.
keyVerses.significance: This verse highlights Ezra’s expertise in the Mosaic Law and God’s favor upon him, evidenced by the king granting his requests. It underscores the divine enabling behind Ezra’s mission and the importance of God’s law in Israel’s restoration.

keyVerses.text: For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the LORD, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments.
keyVerses.significance: This verse reveals Ezra’s spiritual dedication and purpose: to study, obey, and teach God’s law. It encapsulates the chapter’s theme of covenant renewal and the central role of Scripture in Israel’s identity and governance.

keyVerses.text: And I, even I Artaxerxes the king, do make a decree to all the treasurers which are beyond the river, that whatsoever Ezra the priest, the scribe of the law of the God of heaven, shall require of you, it be done speedily,
keyVerses.significance: This verse demonstrates the king’s official support and authority granted to Ezra, emphasizing the political backing for religious reform. It shows God’s providence in using secular authority to accomplish His purposes.

keyVerses.text: Blessed be the LORD God of our fathers, which hath put such a thing as this in the king's heart, to beautify the house of the LORD which is in Jerusalem:
keyVerses.significance: Ezra’s blessing acknowledges God’s sovereign hand in moving the king’s heart to support the temple’s restoration. It affirms God’s providential control over earthly rulers for His redemptive plans.

characters.name: Ezra
characters.description: A priest and skilled scribe, Ezra is the central figure in this chapter. He is dedicated to the Law of Moses and is divinely empowered to lead a group of Israelites back to Jerusalem to restore proper worship and governance.

characters.name: Artaxerxes
characters.description: King of Persia who issues a royal decree supporting Ezra’s mission. His political authority and resources enable the religious reforms in Jerusalem, illustrating God’s use of secular rulers to accomplish His purposes.

characters.name: The LORD God of Israel
characters.description: Though not directly speaking, God’s providential hand is evident throughout the chapter, granting Ezra favor, moving the king’s heart, and guiding the restoration efforts.

themes.description: God’s sovereign hand is evident in moving the king’s heart and granting Ezra favor, demonstrating that God orchestrates political and spiritual events to fulfill His covenant promises.

Ezra’s commitment to the Law of Moses as the foundation for Israel’s spiritual and civil life underscores the centrality of Scripture for God’s people, a theme crucial for Israel’s identity and restoration.
Ezra exemplifies godly leadership by preparing his heart to seek, obey, and teach God’s law, highlighting the importance of spiritual integrity and wisdom in guiding God’s people.
The chapter marks a significant step in Israel’s post-exilic restoration, focusing on rebuilding not only the temple but also the spiritual and judicial life of the community under God’s law.

historicalContext: Ezra 7 is set during the reign of Artaxerxes I of Persia (circa 458 BC), a period when the Persian Empire controlled the former Babylonian territories, including Judah. The Jewish exiles were permitted to return to Jerusalem to rebuild the temple and re-establish their religious practices. The Persian kings often supported local religious leaders to maintain order and loyalty within their vast empire. Ezra’s journey from Babylon to Jerusalem reflects the broader historical movement of the Jewish people returning from exile, seeking to restore their covenant relationship with God through adherence to the Mosaic Law. The official decree from Artaxerxes demonstrates the political backing necessary for such a religious and social reform in a foreign empire.

theologicalInterpretations.description: Reformed theology emphasizes God’s sovereign providence in raising up Ezra as a faithful minister of the Word, highlighting the centrality of Scripture in covenant renewal and the necessity of godly leadership for church and society.

Dispensationalists see Ezra’s mission as part of God’s unfolding plan for Israel, focusing on the literal restoration of the Jewish people and their land as a distinct program before the full establishment of the Messianic kingdom.

Early church interpreters often viewed Ezra as a type of Christ, a faithful scribe who restores God’s law and leads God’s people back to spiritual purity, emphasizing the importance of teaching and obedience to God’s Word.

Commands for the king to have a copy of the law to read and obey, paralleling Ezra’s role as a scribe dedicated to the Law of Moses.

The discovery and reading of the Book of the Law during Josiah’s reign, a precursor to Ezra’s reforms emphasizing covenant renewal.
Paul’s teaching on submission to governing authorities aligns with the cooperation between Ezra and King Artaxerxes.

application: Commit your heart to seek, obey, and teach God’s Word as Ezra did, making Scripture central in your life and community.
Pray for God’s providential guidance and favor in your responsibilities, trusting He moves hearts and circumstances for His purposes.
Support and respect godly leadership that upholds biblical truth and justice within the church and society.
Use your resources generously to support the work of God’s kingdom, following the example of the king’s offerings to the temple.
Be diligent in learning and applying God’s statutes, recognizing their role in personal holiness and communal order.
conclusion: Ezra Chapter 7 stands as a powerful testimony to God’s providential care in restoring His people through faithful leadership and obedience to His Word. Ezra’s dedication to the Law of Moses, combined with the king’s political support, marks a crucial moment of spiritual renewal for Israel. For believers today, this chapter encourages wholehearted commitment to Scripture, reliance on God’s guidance, and active participation in the work of God’s kingdom, reminding us that God sovereignly orchestrates history to accomplish His redemptive purposes.
